metadata.source: Per-region climate.md dossiers + national/regional climate-projection sources (CMIP6 SSP2-4.5, IPMA, AEMET, Meteo-France DRIAS, Met Office UKCP18, NCA5, Ouranos, WICCI, etc.)
metadata.source_url: see per-feature `source_url` for the primary source
metadata.vintage: 2026-05 compilation; per-feature source vintages 2020-2025; re-verified and extended to 30 regions 2026-10
metadata.license: Research dossiers internal; underlying climate-projection sources are typically open government / publicly funded
metadata.note: Buffering is a description of how much a place cushions heat and drought, never a score of how good a place is. Delivers Overview decision 8.1's 'climate-buffering features (altitude, distance-to-coast, mountain-shelter exposure)' as a structured per-jurisdiction layer. Pairs the static buffering features with the dynamic trajectory_under_warming so the layer surfaces both 'how resilient is the microclimate' and 'how fast is it being eroded.'

properties.buffering_notes: Dossier describes Alentejo as one of the hotter, drier corners of Europe with no buffering features named in climate.md.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: extreme summer heat and drought
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +2.7 to 2.9C warming envelope per IPMA, with summer warming of +2.0 to 2.5C and 10 to 15% reduction in wet-day frequency by 2041 to 2060.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); Soares et al. Scientific Reports 2024; IPMA Climate Scenarios 2023; Gomes et al. 2024
properties.gaps: No explicit altitude band or microclimate-buffering feature discussed.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md identifies Galicia as a partial climate refugium in IPCC AR6, buffered against extreme heat by Atlantic maritime influence.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: more intense winter storms and AMOC-shift tail risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +1.5 to 2.0C by mid-century, more modest than Iberian interior; summer heat unlikely to become a primary stress this century.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); AEMET 2023; MDPI Land 14:85 (2025)
properties.gaps: No specific altitude range given for coastal versus interior placement.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md cites elevation, forest cover, and continental setting as providing partial buffering; high-elevation Carpathian valleys are EEA-flagged refugia.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: forest-pathogen and bark-beetle outbreaks in spruce monocultures
properties.trajectory_notes: Summer warming of +2.5 to 3.0C by 2050 over 1961-1990 baseline; heatwave frequency in Romanian lowlands roughly tripled since 1990s with uplands trending similarly.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); Bojariu et al. Springer 2014; World Bank CCKP Romania
properties.gaps: Plateau-versus-Carpathian-flank altitude bands not differentiated in detail.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md describes Atlantic-maritime climate that drifts rather than transforms with no projected heat-stress regime change; water.md and soil.md document blanket peat storing ~240 t C/ha and deep raised bogs storing up to 3,000 t C/ha with order-of-magnitude reliable summer flow.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: Atlantic storm intensification and AMOC-shift tail risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +0.7 to 1.5C by mid-century, among the slowest-warming regions in Europe; no projected drought, heat, or fire regime change.
properties.source: EPA Research 471 (2023); Met Eireann 2024; ICHEC 2023; WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: Altitude range for building placement not specified; AMOC-shift probability not quantified.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md frames west Wales as a relatively stable maritime climate with mild winters (Jan min 3-4C) and moderate summers (July max 19-21C) thanks to Atlantic exposure.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: intense hourly rainfall and flash-flood risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Hourly rainfall extremes above 20 mm/h projected to become roughly 4x more frequent by 2070s under high emissions; +1.2 to 1.8C mean warming by mid-century.
properties.source: Met Office UKCP18; PMC9992391 (2023); World Bank CCKP UK
properties.gaps: Altitude range not specified; coastal cliff versus inland buffering not differentiated.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md identifies Mont Lozere, Aigoual, and Mejean plateau as elevation-mediated climate refugia where mean July maxima at 1500 m remain ~22-24C even under +2C global warming.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: cevenol autumn flash-flood storms with debris-flow risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Southern France warming above the national +1.7 to 2.7C trajectory; maximum daily autumn precipitation up ~30% since mid-20th century; summer precipitation projected down 15 to 25% by 2050.
properties.source: Meteo-France DRIAS 2024; WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: Lower-slope versus high-plateau microclimate boundaries not mapped quantitatively.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md describes a 1000-metre altitudinal gradient as a climate-selection lever; a settlement at 1000 m today experiences a climate similar to the Bolzano valley floor of 1950.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: glacier-fed irrigation baseflow loss and debris flows
properties.trajectory_notes: Alpine warming roughly twice the global mean; Ortles-Cevedale and Stubai glaciers lost over 30% of 1980 ice volume by 2024; more debris flows and convective storms since 2000.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); Bucchignani et al. Scientific Data 2023; Crespi et al. Scientific Reports 2020; EURAC
properties.gaps: Valley-inversion frequency and cold-air-pooling sites not enumerated.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md frames Asturias as buffered against extreme heat by Atlantic maritime influence with an abrupt coast-to-Cordillera-Cantabrica gradient and IPCC-recognised cool-temperate refugia above 1000 m.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: intense Atlantic storms and AMOC-shift tail risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +1.5 to 2.0C by mid-century; Atlantic regime moderates the broader Spanish 14 to 20% rainfall decline projected for 2050.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); AEMET 2023; MDPI Land 14:85 (2025)
properties.gaps: Specific upper altitude limit for habitable buffering not stated.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md flags the central loess plain as exposed within Germany's primary inland-drought zone (Mitteldeutsches Trockengebiet); only the Harz foothills offer some microclimate variability.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: summer drought and groundwater drawdown
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +1.8 to 2.5C by mid-century with pronounced drying trend; 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2022 summers already caused major agricultural impacts.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); DWD; PMC11322161 (2024); World Bank CCKP Germany
properties.gaps: Harz-foothill altitude buffering not quantified; only flagged qualitatively.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md notes Saaremaa coastal sites are 2-3C warmer in winter than mainland southeast due to Baltic moderation, with less snow but more wind-storm exposure.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: shrinking winter snow regime and Baltic Sea ecosystem shifts
properties.trajectory_notes: Northern latitudes amplify warming; +2.0 to 2.5C by mid-century, with Baltic SST projected +2 to 4C by 2100; growing season expands 2 to 4 weeks.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); Estonian Weather Service; World Bank CCKP Estonia; PMC4447695 (2015)
properties.gaps: Estonia is low-altitude with no mountain buffering; dossier does not give an altitude range.

properties.buffering_notes: WorldClim 17-GCM SSP2-4.5 mean annual temperature 8.6 C for 2041-2060 over the footprint (7.2 C in 1970-2000), cool and oceanic with a 4-883 m elevation spread; blanket peat covers much of the ground (SoilGrids 0-30 cm carbon mean 305 g/kg), though its water-storage role was not measured here.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: heavier winter rain on steep, peaty ground (flood and landslip), drier summers and more frequent drought, and wildfire; magnitudes for this footprint not opened
properties.trajectory_notes: Adaptation Scotland's UKCP18 summary (RCP-based, August 2025): Scottish winter rainfall +11 percent by 2050 on a high pathway (10th-90th percentile -19 to +44), larger in the west; summer rainfall -8 percent; snow losses smaller in the mountains than low ground. About +1.4 C in the WorldClim ensemble against 1970-2000.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1; Adaptation Scotland, Climate Projections for Scotland - Summary (Met Office UKCP18, August 2025)
properties.gaps: Flood, landslip and wildfire magnitudes for the footprint, peat depth and Highland-specific UKCP18 values were not opened.

properties.altitude_range_m: 72-296 (Global Solar Atlas elevation at 318 sample points; summits and fells are higher)
properties.buffering_notes: FMI describes North Karelia as a continental province split between a thermally favourable lake region (Höytiäinen, Pyhäselkä, Pielinen valley) and barren watershed uplands, and Kainuu as typically continental: annual mean 1991-2020 about +2 to +4 C in North Karelia, large seasonal swings, harsh frosts and heat spells under Russian high pressure. Lakes and the peat that covers 32 to 45 percent of forestry land store water and moderate local temperature.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: shorter snow season and milder, wetter winters
properties.trajectory_notes: FMI (CMIP5 RCP scenarios, context only): warming of about 1.8-5.6 C in North Karelia and 1.9-5.8 C in Kainuu this century against 1981-2010, largest from November to March; precipitation +6 to +16% (North Karelia) and +6 to +17% (Kainuu); 1991-2020 already about 0.6 C warmer than 1981-2010. Snow depth in mid-March is 50-70 cm now (70-80 cm on the uplands). WorldClim SSP2-4.5 2041-2060 footprint mean is 5.4 C.
properties.source: Finnish Meteorological Institute ilmasto-opas: Pohjois-Karjala and Kainuu regional climate articles (updated 2022); WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: Spruce bark-beetle and forest-damage stress named in pre-research was not verified; FMI scenarios are CMIP5-based and cannot be relabelled SSP2-4.5.

properties.buffering_notes: Plateau of 300 to 1,000 m (Parc); about 20% of the Parc is wetland and 3.4% peatland (Parc), rainfall 800 to 1,600 mm a year, forest about half the area. Footprint mean temperature in the 1970-2000 normal was 9.7 C (cells 8.4 to 11.3).
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: repeated summer droughts (named by the Parc) and the climate risks its forest charter lists: water resource, fire access, dieback
properties.trajectory_notes: WorldClim 17-GCM mean for 2041-2060 under SSP2-4.5 is 12.0 C against 9.7 C in 1970-2000: +2.3 C (individual GCMs +1.4 to +3.6). Rainfall projections were not opened.
properties.source: WorldClim 2.1 (historical and CMIP6) zonal means; Parc naturel régional de Millevaches (aquatic milieux; forest charter)
properties.gaps: No precipitation or drought-index projection opened; fire and dieback risk named by the Parc but not quantified.

properties.buffering_notes: Mean temperature in the footprint is about 10.3 C (1970-2000) against warmer lowlands within 120-150 km (Zaragoza, Valencia); the 640-1,700 m relief gives cold winters and cooler summers than the Ebro valley and the coast. Altitude is the only buffer named here: the interior has no sea or lake influence, and it swings between cold winters and hot dry summers.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: drought and wildfire on a water-short, warming upland (WorldClim +2.5 C by 2041-2060 on 1970-2000; Aqueduct 2050 extremely high; Aliaga fire 2009: 7,301 ha)
properties.trajectory_notes: Footprint mean 10.3 C (1970-2000) to 12.7 C (2041-2060, SSP2-4.5, 17 GCMs; range 11.9-13.7); the marker cell goes from 11.1 to 13.6 C. The altitude margin against the hot Ebro and Valencian lowlands persists but erodes, and water and fire are the binding limits, not heat.
properties.source: WorldClim 2.1 (1970-2000) and CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 2041-2060, computed 2026-10-04; WRI Aqueduct 4.0; Hansen GFC v1.11
properties.gaps: AEMET and AdapteCCa regional scenarios not opened; no frost-day or heat-day indices; altitude as the only named buffering feature (no coast, lake or large forest-canopy claim verified).

properties.altitude_range_m: 543-2,923 m (sampled at 107 grid points; summits are higher)
properties.buffering_notes: Lapse rate about 0.59 C per 100 m in WorldClim 2041-2060 cells: the 500-1,500 m band where people live is about 11.9 C against 8.2 C for the whole valley, and 3.8 C above 2,200 m. Newcomers in Pettenati's study settled sunny-slope borgate (solana) away from the main road.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: Summer drought, heavy-rain flooding and heat are the local risks to watch; ARPA Piemonte calls the Alps a climate-change 'hotspot' (warming above the global trend) and its scenarios show wetter winters and drier summers
properties.trajectory_notes: WorldClim 17-GCM SSP2-4.5: +2.5 C between 1970-2000 and 2041-2060 over the footprint (settlement band 9.3 to 11.9 C). ARPA Piemonte scenarios: about +2 C by 2100 under RCP4.5, more above 700 m; winter precipitation +10-15 percent, summer drying up to 30 percent under RCP8.5. Recent local flood and landslide events (including October 2020) not verified.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (computed); ARPA Piemonte, Scenari climatici futuri in Piemonte and Impatti del cambiamento climatico; Pettenati 2013
properties.gaps: Aspect (solana versus ombra) and valley-inversion frequency not quantified; observed Maira discharge and snow-line trend not opened; Oct 2020 event not verified.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md cites an NCA5 projection that the Pacific Northwest will have the fewest very-hot days of any contiguous US region through 2060, because marine airflow in western Cascadia buffers inland heat; this was not checked against the chapter text (not verified).
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: late-summer wildfire smoke and heat-dome tail risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +1.5 to 2.0C by mid-century; 2021 heat dome (Portland 46.7C) attribution studies indicate such events become 2-3x more likely by 2060; AQI above 150 days increasing.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); NCA5 Chapter 27; PRISM 1991-2020; Philip et al. WWA 2022
properties.gaps: Willamette Valley altitude band not given numerically.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md describes Vermont as wet, green, and free of heat-stress extremes; the design-relevant risk is precipitation intensity rather than thermal collapse.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: flash flooding on river-bottomlands per Irene 2011 and 2023 events
properties.trajectory_notes: NCA5 names the Northeast as the fastest-warming region in the contiguous US; +1.7 to 2.5C by mid-century with heat-index above 38C tripling by mid-century.
properties.source: NOAA NCEI 1991-2020; Vermont Climate Assessment 2021 (UVM Gund); NCA5 Chapter 21; WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: Specific altitude buffering bands for the Green Mountains not enumerated in climate.md.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md credits Asheville's ~670 m elevation for holding the baseline MAT to 13.5C and notes Appalachian highland zones track the lower end of the regional warming range due to elevation buffering; ridges shelter from Gulf tropical systems.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: extreme-precipitation flash flooding per Tropical Storm Helene 2024
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +1.5 to 2.0C mean warming by mid-century; extreme-heat days above 31.8C projected to rise from ~7/yr to ~45/yr by 2050; annual precipitation rising from ~940 to ~1215 mm.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); NCA5 Chapter 22; NOAA NCEI; NC Climate Office; ClimateCheck 2025
properties.gaps: Upper altitude range and ridge-specific buffering not quantified.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md notes the karst and deep-coulee topography handles intense rain events better than flat tilled land but does not describe explicit thermal-buffering features.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: precipitation volatility with more intense rain interspersed with dry spells
properties.trajectory_notes: WICCI projects +2.3C statewide warming by 2041-2060 with 90F+ days rising from 9 to 26 per year; trajectory called the most benign in the framework but still substantial.
properties.source: Wisconsin State Climatology Office; WICCI 2024; NCA5 Great Lakes Chapter; WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: Coulee-versus-ridge thermal differential not quantified; no altitude range given.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md states ridgeline and plateau sites at 500-700 m run 3-5C cooler than valley floors in summer, extending the comfortable working season.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: intensifying dry-spell to flood cycle with diminishing summer baseflow
properties.trajectory_notes: Projected +2.0 to 2.5C above 1991-2020 by mid-century, pushing the region firmly into humid subtropical territory; days above 38C roughly doubling.
properties.source: NOAA NCEI 1991-2020; NWS Tulsa; NOAA NCICS Arkansas 2022; NCA5 Chapter 22; KSMU 2025
properties.gaps: Specific ridge versus valley microclimate maps not in dossier.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md frames the 2100 m elevation as the region's greatest climate asset and also its greatest illusion, currently below physiological heat danger but eroding fast.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: landscape-scale wildfire per Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon 2022
properties.trajectory_notes: New Mexico warmed 1.85C between 1970 and 2018, the fastest of any contiguous US state; the NOAA State Climate Summary for New Mexico (2022) says annual average temperatures are projected to most likely exceed historical record levels by the middle of this century even under a lower emissions pathway.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 (2024); NOAA NCEI State Climate Summary, New Mexico (2022); Sillmann et al. ESEv 2022; 350newmexico.org
properties.gaps: Sangre de Cristo upper altitude limits for habitable buffering not exhaustively given.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md identifies the Atlantic Ocean as regulating temperature year-round, keeping the feels-like summer ceiling substantially lower than continental interior comparators like Ottawa or Montreal.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: intensifying noreasters, ice storms, and emerging wildfire risk
properties.trajectory_notes: Provincial projection of +2.6C by mid-century lifting MAT toward 9.3C; 2023 Upper Tantallon and 2025 fires were the province's most destructive on record; the +2.6C figure behind the 9.3C mean annual temperature could not be read on the replacement source (not verified).
properties.source: ClimateData.ca (replaces the provincial Changing Climate page, which blocks scripted requests); WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1; ECCC normals
properties.gaps: Cape Breton Highlands altitude band quantified only as 1-2C colder than provincial mean.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md calls the altitudinal gradient the region's most valuable climate-adaptation lever; a settlement at 900 m today experiences roughly what the valley floor experienced in the 1970s.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: mega-fire season and shrinking glacial summer baseflow
properties.trajectory_notes: Columbia Basin projected 2.5 to 3.5C warmer than 1960s by 2050s; 2023 BC fire season burned over 2.84 million ha (more than double any prior year) with Drought Level 5 in the Kootenays.
properties.source: ClimateNA / AdaptWest CMIP6 SSP2-4.5; Nelson Climate Profile 2022; ClimateData.ca; BC Wildfire Service 2023
properties.gaps: Glacier-loss timing relative to settlement horizons not fully resolved.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md describes Estrie as a moderate climate zone with reliable snowpack feeding spring soil moisture across rolling Appalachian terrain, but no explicit mountain-shelter or coastal-moderation feature.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: rising flash-flood risk from precipitation intensity
properties.trajectory_notes: Ouranos projects +2 to 3C for southern Quebec under SSP3-7.0 with SSP2-4.5 at the low end (~2C); frost-free period lengthens 2 to 3 weeks; growing season net-positive for regen operations.
properties.source: Environment Canada 1981-2010 Normals; Ouranos CMIP6 / ESPO-G6-R2; WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: Altitude band of the southern Appalachian foothills not numerically given.

properties.buffering_notes: Climate.md calls altitude the primary site-selection variable; a Sierra Norte settlement at 1800-2500 m gains 2-4C of thermal buffer and remains temperate through 2050 under SSP2-4.5, arguably the most climate-resilient band in the North American regen landscape.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: intensifying dry season requiring storage and fog-harvest
properties.trajectory_notes: South-southeast Mexico projected +1.5 to 2.0C by 2041-2060 with dry-season (March-May) temperatures warming fastest at +1.8C; Oaxaca named among states with most high-exposure municipalities.
properties.source: Vazquez-Aguirre et al. MDPI Climate 11(5):111 (2023); WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1; World Bank CCKP Mexico
properties.gaps: Cloud-forest fog-belt elevation not quantified beyond night-frost above 2500 m.

properties.buffering_notes: Cayuga (133 m) and Seneca (188 m) lakes are among the deepest in the US; per Wikipedia their lake effect retains summer warmth in winter and winter cold in spring. Footprint elevation 73-607 m (Global Solar Atlas sample). Forest cover is 42 percent of the footprint (Hansen, canopy 30 percent or more). Pre-research claim tested: water stress is very low (0.015) but 2041-2060 mean temperature (11.2 C) is mid-slate and no drought or heat-day dataset was opened, so 'less heat-and-drought-exposed' is only partly supported.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: heavy rain and flash flooding: NCA5 reports Northeast extreme precipitation events up about 60 percent, the largest increase in the US
properties.trajectory_notes: WorldClim mean annual temperature 8.1 C (1970-2000) to 11.2 C (2041-2060, SSP2-4.5 17-GCM mean), +3.1 C; Aqueduct 2050 BAU stress 0.0149 vs baseline 0.0127.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1 and WorldClim 2.1 historical; NCA5 Chapter 21; Wikipedia, Finger Lakes; Hansen GFC v1.11
properties.gaps: Heat-day and drought indices; flood-zone mapping; lake-effect quantification (4 km grid cannot resolve it).

properties.altitude_range_m: 68-171 (Global Solar Atlas elevation at 59 footprint points)
properties.buffering_notes: Low, rolling Piedmont with 70% tree cover (Hansen year-2000 canopy 30% or more); no altitude, coastal or lake moderation of note. The Blue Ridge lies to the west, outside the footprint.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: heat and extreme rainfall; NOAA names severe thunderstorms, tropical storms, hurricanes, drought and heat waves for Virginia; the 2011 M5.8 earthquake was centred in Louisa County (not a climate signal)
properties.trajectory_notes: WorldClim SSP2-4.5 ensemble 16.1 C by 2041-2060 against about 14.3 C today; NOAA State Climate Summary 2022: more intense droughts and more frequent extreme heat and extreme precipitation projected; cold waves less intense.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1; NOAA NCEI State Climate Summaries 2022, Virginia; Global Solar Atlas
properties.gaps: No hurricane-remnant or flood-zone analysis; Virginia Climate Center not opened.

properties.altitude_range_m: 0 to about 930 (Global Solar Atlas elevations at 315 sample points; p10-p90 134-484 m)
properties.buffering_notes: 84% of the footprint was forest of 30% canopy or more in 2000 (Hansen) and the foothill ridges rise to about 930 m. Coastal moderation by the estuary is plausible but was not measured or sourced, so it is not listed as a feature.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: Warming of about 3.3 °C from the 1970-2000 baseline (2.0 °C) to 2041-2060 (5.3 °C, SSP2-4.5 ensemble), and a spruce-budworm outbreak mapped here from 2012 (9,436 ha) and 2013 (61,184 ha) alongside canopy loss that rose about 60% after 2013
properties.trajectory_notes: Observed state plus trajectory: Hansen forest loss 0.37-0.84% a year in 2001-2012 and 0.51-1.03% a year in 2013-2023 (net -3.4 %/decade); Ouranos gives +2 to 3 °C by 2050 for southern Québec under SSP3-7.0 relative to 1991-2020. Winter warming, freeze-thaw, estuary ice-cover loss and coastal erosion (an expectation from pre-research) were not verified from an opened source and are left out.
properties.source: WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1; Hansen GFC v1.11; MRNF Québec spruce budworm aerial survey; Ouranos
properties.gaps: Estuary ice-cover, coastal erosion and winter-warming figures for Bas-Saint-Laurent not sourced; WorldClim baseline period (1970-2000) differs from Ouranos' (1991-2020).

properties.buffering_notes: Continental interior, 150 to 325 m (Global Solar Atlas elevation at 179 footprint points; mean 235 m), with no coast, mountains or large lake. Tree cover is only 23.5 percent of the footprint (Hansen, year 2000), so canopy buffering is patchy.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: mean annual temperature rising about 3.3 C by 2041-2060 on a flat-to-dissected continental landscape; precipitation baseline 940 mm per year (WorldClim 1970-2000)
properties.trajectory_notes: WorldClim 1970-2000 baseline BIO1 10.7 C over the footprint; CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 2041-2060 17-model mean 13.9 C (models 12.4 to 15.3). Rainfall extremes, flood and drought swings are the pre-research expectation and were not verified here.
properties.source: WorldClim v2.1 baseline and CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 (computed); Global Solar Atlas elevation; Hansen GFC v1.11
properties.gaps: Heavy-rain, flood and drought statistics from state climatologists not retrieved; NCA5 Midwest chapter host did not resolve.

properties.altitude_range_m: 5-222 (Global Solar Atlas elevation at 160 land sample points)
properties.buffering_notes: A cold-water coast (Gulf of Maine and Bay of Fundy) and a county that is about 93% forest by area (Hansen year-2000 canopy of 30% or more) hold WorldClim's 2041-2060 mean annual temperature to 9.0 C (17-GCM mean, range 7.8 to 10.7). The coastal-versus-inland gradient (fog, summer highs) was not quantified from a primary source, so strength is rated moderate.
properties.primary_vulnerability_signal: sea-level rise and storm-surge flooding on the coast (Machias tide gauge during the 10 and 13 January 2024 storms), a Gulf of Maine warming nearly three times faster than the world ocean, hydrologic drought and well stress, and rising tick-borne disease
properties.trajectory_notes: Maine has warmed about 3.5 F since the late 1800s and the 10 warmest years on record have all occurred since 1998; annual precipitation +15% over the last century; sea level rise rate along four tide gauges (including Eastport) is 75% faster in 1996-2025 than over the long record; Lyme disease, anaplasmosis and babesiosis cases have risen in Maine (Maine had the third-highest Lyme rate in 2023 per US CDC). The Gulf of Maine has cooled somewhat in the past couple of years: STS calls this a pause in warming, not a reversal. GMRI: 0.84 F per decade 1982-2024 against 0.3 F for the world ocean.
properties.source: Maine Climate Council Scientific and Technical Subcommittee, 2026 Interim Climate Science Report; Gulf of Maine Research Institute, 2024 Gulf of Maine Warming Update; WorldClim CMIP6 v2.1
properties.gaps: No county-scale projection from the Maine Climate Council; coastal-versus-inland temperature gradient and fog frequency not quantified; Eastport and Lubec surge exposure maps not opened.
